title: Contact
metaDescription: Reach out about your Montana mineral rights. No obligation, no pressure, and a direct response from the person who actually reviews your documents.
heroLead: Reaching out doesn't commit you to anything. It starts a conversation about what you actually own and whether selling makes sense for your situation.
intro: Most owners who contact me have a specific question before they have a decision made: what's a fair number, what does my royalty statement actually mean, or what do I even own after inheriting this interest from a relative. That's a fine place to start. You don't need a firm decision to reach out, and you won't be pressured into one.
Below is what actually happens once you send a message, so there are no surprises about the process.

sections.heading: What Happens After You Reach Out
paragraphs: I read every message personally rather than routing it through a call center or a team of junior staff, and I respond directly, usually within a business day or two. If you've included your county and a general sense of what you own, I'll let you know what additional documents, if any, would help me put together a real, tract-specific offer rather than a generic range.

If your situation is complicated, unresolved heirship, unclear title, a mix of producing and non-producing interests, I'll tell you honestly what that means for timeline rather than promising something unrealistic just to keep the conversation moving.

sections.heading: What To Have Ready
paragraphs: It helps to know your county, and if you have it, your decimal interest or net mineral acres. If the tract is producing, a recent royalty statement speeds things up considerably, since it confirms current activity without me having to estimate. None of this is required to make first contact, though, if you're not sure what you have, that uncertainty is exactly the kind of thing I can help sort through.
If you're contacting me on behalf of a family estate or multiple heirs, it's useful to mention that upfront, since it changes what documentation eventually gets requested.

sections.heading: How I Respond
paragraphs: Every response is personal and specific to what you've shared, not a form letter. If I need more information to give you a useful answer, I'll ask directly rather than sending a vague reply. If your tract is outside what I'd realistically offer on, whether because of location, size, or documentation gaps, I'll say so plainly rather than stringing the conversation along.
You're free to ask questions before providing any documents at all. Plenty of owners start with a general question about how the process works before deciding whether to move forward.

sections.heading: If You're Not Ready To Sell Yet
paragraphs: That's a completely reasonable place to be, and reaching out doesn't obligate you to anything. Some owners contact me a year or more before actually deciding to sell, just to understand what their interest might be worth or what documents they'd eventually need. I'm glad to have that conversation without any pressure toward a faster timeline than makes sense for you.
Whenever you're ready, whether that's this week or next year, the same honest process applies.

sections.heading: Reaching Me From Anywhere
paragraphs: Plenty of the mineral owners I talk to don't live in Montana at all, they live in Washington, Minnesota, or wherever family scattered after the original homesteader passed the interest down. That's completely normal, and it doesn't change how the process works. Whether you're in Billings or three states away, contact happens the same way, by message or by phone, and documents move by mail or courier through the entire process.

If you're contacting me about a relative's interest and you're not the direct owner yet, mention that too. It usually means the estate needs to be settled or an heirship document prepared before a sale can close, and it's better to know that early.

faqs.question: Is there any cost to contacting you?
faqs.answer: No, reaching out and getting a response costs nothing, and there's no obligation attached to the conversation.

faqs.question: What information should I include in my first message?
faqs.answer: Your county, a general description of your interest, and whether it's producing helps me respond with something useful, but even a brief message with none of that is a fine place to start.

faqs.question: How fast will I hear back?
faqs.answer: Typically within a business day or two. If your situation needs more research on my end, I'll let you know that upfront rather than leaving you waiting without an update.

faqs.question: Can I ask general questions without providing my personal documents?
faqs.answer: Yes, plenty of owners start with questions about how the process works, what a royalty statement means, or general value ranges before sharing anything specific about their own interest.

faqs.question: Do you work with owners who live outside Montana?
faqs.answer: Yes, most of the owners I talk to don't live in the state where their minerals sit. Everything can be handled remotely by phone, mail, and courier through closing.

faqs.question: Can I speak with you by phone instead of writing everything out?
faqs.answer: Yes, once initial contact is made, a phone call is often the fastest way to walk through your situation and figure out what documents would actually help.
